---
If you’ve followed election coverage over the last year or so, the pundits might lead you to believe something new is happening.
Despite high disapproval for President Joe Biden in red states like Kentucky and Mississippi, Democrats outperformed their party’s presidential margin in statewide races by double digits. And after Republican-dominated legislatures passed extreme abortion bans in red states like Kansas and Ohio, voters delivered huge wins for reproductive rights and democracy.
But the truth is, this isn’t all that new. While pundits and insiders increasingly divide us into columns of red and blue based on their one-dimensional view of politics, voters continue to confound their expectations in election after election.
Missouri is a great example. While our state has shifted solidly red in presidential preferences since 2012, Democrats have won a half-dozen statewide campaigns, even as recently as 2018. And when Missouri politicians have adopted extreme positions on issues such as abortion, workers’ rights or health care, they’ve often seen their out-of-touch agendas soundly rejected by voters.
**Just like voters in states where we’ve seen big wins for Democrats and pro-freedom initiatives in the past year, hundreds of thousands of voters in Missouri are still splitting their tickets.**
I know this more than most because I’ve lived it. I won a race for Missouri Secretary of State. And in 2016, Missouri’s last Senate race to take place during a presidential election, I fell just 2.8% short of defeating a longtime Republican incumbent for U.S. Senate. And I outperformed the Democratic presidential ticket’s margin by more than 16%.
We proved that in races where well-funded candidates can set themselves apart and make it clear to voters that they’ll fight for them in office, Democrats can win in Missouri.
That’s what we’re seeing in Missouri’s current U.S. Senate race, as my friend Lucas Kunce takes on incumbent Josh Hawley. Much like my race in 2016, 2024 pits a labor-backed veteran against a politician — _except my opponent never tried to overthrow the government violently just to get his name out there._
Now up for reelection in 2024, Hawley faces Lucas, a Marine veteran and antitrust advocate who’s broken fundraising records, rallied Missouri’s election-winning labor movement behind him and built a reputation as a different kind of Democrat who speaks truth to power, regardless of party.
**[I’m proud to support Lucas Kunce in his race against Josh Hawley and I hope you’ll join me by adding a donation of $10 or whatever you’re able to today. My entire life has been guided by the conviction that America is a beacon of liberty, freedom, and democracy.
_Donald Trump is an existential threat to every fundamental American value._
He won't defend democracy. He's a dangerous mob leader who attacked the foundation of our nation, encouraging a violent group of supporters to march on the Capitol to prevent the peaceful transfer of power.

Believe me, if I didn’t have to, I wouldn’t. But Christi Jacobsen has a pretty sizable war chest that she’ll deploy this fall to keep herself in office. She’s gotten closer with election deniers, she didn’t fix a website bug that was double charging small business owners to remain in good standing, and she generally doesn’t seem all that interested in executing her duties as SoS. So I'm asking one last time before the end of the month: [**can you chip in $5 or $10 to my campaign to help me defeat Jacobsen?**](http://links.mullenformontana.com/u/click?_t=96962950e68f455895e83c6431fce0d7&_m=267575da009d4a75b3d958c66810d388&_e=ULBy4lGbdTwpbnwbLyXbJhLmVUjddT82nCjso8jwmJBbVbO4_UV_W8WA-EM4aSXVlIqMuWywN1skcaSaiDcT3E3zUgFD49m3ia5kbDUXU6vACtesr_uIzkwZG6slHpCR0wFNPaFs4jphnGrRxbHuj8h2N5EJytwtGqoqhQ6V0l2zWHSy8K43UwCeGs6R6j-4lZepskGUsOhranEf6kI-7xgvi08tbnRPhPVXTTJAFKwBbg7bA5ve0fcFw8-s21ggC63cOp28VGGsP5PkFkuztQsTHZrJBdJg5z1Z4R4Mia6RVipCla899yQGhGM5aZ6iJyT63NsCs9pwTne7afO1kYRpNPwjtnnjQhA0UO73Q9XWR-1nCB6XmNoYi0ve4yO1gbJNNLf7CuKqkxd_N2FW-6WxGPozEPKYmJRdW_u4j7Q%3D) [DONATE TODAY](http://links.mullenformontana.com/u/click?_t=96962950e68f455895e83c6431fce0d7&_m=267575da009d4a75b3d958c66810d388&_e=ULBy4lGbdTwpbnwbLyXbJhLmVUjddT82nCjso8jwmJBbVbO4_UV_W8WA-EM4aSXVlIqMuWywN1skcaSaiDcT3E3zUgFD49m3ia5kbDUXU6vACtesr_uIzkwZG6slHpCR0wFNPaFs4jphnGrRxbHuj8h2N5EJytwtGqoqhQ6V0l2zWHSy8K43UwCeGs6R6j-4lZepskGUsOhranEf6kI-7xgvi08tbnRPhPVXTTJAFKwBbg7bA5ve0fcFw8-s21gg7PGAMimj7rZYQs-bn_ETrv5g2IwDTa-FTVaXBK0Ly_MFYmoEg9pOUMeaTdyGTNQNiacL0BKTnuhaVzO6gracCD0LGUkXmdE0ip-VK4k81qvsS0MGd58sLeWM6U0aMl9lWl0_c-Rg4m7vXGyb8s7ToAWWhZg_dkUs8Swqu-h7WIw%3D) As a small business owner myself, I understand the challenges that come with the territory. body:
The Washington Post just reported on a leaked poll from the National Republican Senatorial Committee.

| Peter, we’ll keep this short.

The Washington Post just reported on a leaked poll from the National Republican Senatorial Committee.

Kari Lake leads Ruben by 1% in that poll — the first time she’s beaten Ruben in publicly available polling since February.

Bad. Bad, bad, bad.

There’s a lot that needs to happen to turn this around. First and foremost, we need to get back on track to our goals. If we do not raise what we need to win this race Kari Lake is going to hold and expand this lead.

He said they needed to “know that here in America we are waging a great and successful war. It is not alone a war against want and destitution and economic demoralization. It is more than that; it is a war for the survival of democracy. We are fighting to save a great and precious form of government for ourselves and for the world.”
That is our fight today. To not only defend our democracy from the Donald Trumps and the David Schweikerts, but to show the world that American democracy works. **[Will you join the fight by donating to our campaign before our FEC deadline?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/87730530/482073545/-1561725702?amount=10&refcode=AU_AHC_FR_GEN_EOQ_AC_20240627_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDUwMDAiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOWYzZmIxMWUtYjYzNC1lZjExLTg2ZDItNjA0NWJkZDllMDk2IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=mlgrXA6NIJ5QM-CrWSaellNED8RFuHA5FfyJBw1Mosg=)**
We can show the world that when 80% of Americans want common sense gun laws or comprehensive immigration reform or tax fairness, the voice of the people and not special interests will rule the day.
That we live in our country where women have the freedom to get the help they need to become pregnant or not to become pregnant, that parents can check out the books of their choosing for their kids from the library, that we can marry those we love.
That the rule of law applies to all – no matter whether they are selling drugs on a street corner or crooked executives in a corner office or a former president in the Oval Office.
We need to show the world that America is a place where hard work and not just wealth is valued and rewarded.

And there’s no debate about this: AZ-01 is the only congressional district in America that could end up deciding who controls the House, the Senate, and the White House. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | = = | = = | = = That evening in 1936, FDR made clear what he was fighting for. Though it was three years before the beginning of World War II, he said there were people around the world who had lost their democracy and freedoms and “only our success can stir their ancient hope.” He said they needed to “know that here in America we are waging a great and successful war. It is not alone a war against want and destitution and economic demoralization. It is more than that; it is a war for the survival of democracy. We are fighting to save a great and precious form of government for ourselves and for the world.” That is our fight today. To not only defend our democracy from the Donald Trumps and the David Schweikerts, but to show the world that American democracy works. = We can show the world that when 80% of Americans want common sense gun laws or comprehensive immigration reform or tax fairness, the voice of the people and not special interests will rule the day. That we live in our country where women have the freedom to get the help they need to become pregnant or not to become pregnant, that parents can check out the books of their choosing for their kids from the library, that we can marry those we love. That the rule of law applies to all – no matter whether they are selling drugs on a street corner or crooked executives in a corner office or a former president in the Oval Office. We need to show the world that America is a place where hard work and not just wealth is valued and rewarded. = That's what our fight is for. I believe we will meet our rendezvous with destiny. But I need your help. body:
It's June, so that means we're right around the corner from our important Federal Election Commission deadline.
It's June, so that means we're right around the corner from our important Federal Election Commission deadline: On June 30th, we have an "end-of-quarter" deadline closing our “Q2,” which is the second quarter of the election year.
This will be the last FEC fundraising deadline before the Republican National Convention, beginning on July 15, and before we learn who our Republican opponent will be ahead of the primary on August 6th. It’s also the first deadline since we launched our TV and digital ads.
So it's a biggie. The most important of the campaign to date.
I know campaigns say that a lot, and you deserve to know why it's so important — especially since we're going to be sending a lot of emails about it. Let me show you a perfect embodiment of how these FEC deadlines translate into a report card on our campaign.
See this tweet from a Detroit News bureau chief?
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jf-email-20240627?refcode=em20240627&amount=5&refcode2=9161_434096_-PtZFM&akid=9161%2E434096%2E-PtZFM)
It's from after the last quarterly FEC fundraising deadline reports were filed, after March 31st.
Everyone looks at them. The press, our opponents, and especially outside spending entities looking to see if we are vulnerable to attack as they decide where to allocate their resources.
For us, if we file a good report, maybe some of those super PACs decide to move on from our race. File a bad report, and all bets are off.
Add to that the fact that the fundraising goals we set for these FEC deadlines are not arbitrary. They are important benchmarks we have to meet in order to keep our ads on the air and continue reaching voters. They are what we need to raise in order to win.
So yes, this is the most important FEC fundraising deadline of the campaign so far. And yes, our April and May fundraising was less than we had hoped for. So we're really banking on a big month to catch up before we file our report. And we can't do that without people who care enough about the outcome of this race to make a difference. So please:
[**Can I ask you to use this link to make a contribution to our campaign and John Fetterman's before our FEC fundraising deadline on June 30th? Our average online donation is around $30. Some give more. Others give less. But if we get lots and lots of donations of all amounts, we'll reach our goals.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jf-email-20240627?refcode=em20240627&amount=5&refcode2=9161_434096_-PtZFM&akid=9161%2E434096%2E-PtZFM)

Thank you,
Elissa

We must take megaspending from MAGA extremists seriously to protect our movement.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20240627-4039-footer&t=1&akid=4039%2E420207%2EGZUFfR)
Peter, this is a bit of a longer email, but I hope you’ll stick around to the end.
**We must take mega-spending from MAGA extremists seriously to protect our movement.**
On Tuesday, after a deluge of dark money from the GOP and their megadonors, Jamaal Bowman, a member of our progressive movement, lost his primary election.
**This loss is a clear reminder: we cannot afford to lose momentum, slow down our fundraising efforts, or stop growing this movement.** Now more than ever, we must dig deep and show the GOP what we stand for.
There’s no question that the far-right will now feel emboldened in their plans to unseat progressives. And they’re going to try this same tactic on other progressives across the country — **including me and our campaign.**
I’ve got three challengers running against me this time — and I can’t afford to take any chances. Big Super PAC opponents have been polling nasty attack ads against me and I know they’re gearing up to try and take me out. That’s why I’m asking you to help me kick our campaign into high-gear, Peter. We can and will stand up to dark money spending, and we _will_ win our race with you on our side.
In just 3 days, our campaign will face the final FEC fundraising deadline before our primary election — and this will be our _final_ opportunity to fortify our resources before the GOP’s donors turn their sights on us.
I’ve never taken a dime of corporate PAC money and I never will. My campaign is funded through tens of thousands of grassroots donors like you. Now, I need all hands on deck to raise $75,000 before midnight on Sunday so that we can keep fighting at full power while protecting our hard-earned progress. **Can I personally ask you to help kick off our FEC fundraising with a donation of any amount made to the link below?**
[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/pj-email-20230627?personal=dpwillis67@gmail.com](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-email-20240627.WdsvCQ&refcode=em20240627-4039&t=2&akid=4039%2E420207%2EGZUFfR)
Together,
Pramila Jayapal

subject: My plan to fix our democracy

body:

I don’t know about you, but I’m sick and tired of waking up every day in June and waiting on pins and needles to learn whether or not the Supreme Court is going to uphold our rights. I have a plan on how we can restore our democracy so that a small group of right-wing and billionaire-coddling radicals can no longer drown out the will of the people:
* Pass my Judicial Ethics and Anti-Corruption Act, which would make Supreme Court Justices finally follow a basic and enforceable code of ethics.
* Expand the Supreme Court to rebalance it.
* End the filibuster to codify Roe.
* Fix the Electoral College so popular-vote losers like Donald Trump can’t stack the courts again. Remember: Five justices who ended the right to abortion were appointed by presidents who lost the popular vote.

**There are real solutions to the root cause of this crisis but it’s going to take big ideas — and big, structural changes.** [**Add your name if you endorse this plan. To undo the damage done by the right-wing takeover of our federal courts, we must continue to root corruption out of the judiciary and restore our democracy.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-supcourt/?source=EMZ21E_JUD_E_20240627_V1S1&t=8&akid=2245%2E4032634%2EBrZMC7) | [**ADD YOUR NAME**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-supcourt/?source=EMZ21E_JUD_E_20240627_V1S1&t=9&akid=2245%2E4032634%2EBrZMC7)
---
I’ll keep working on immediate next steps — like keeping Joe Biden and Kamala Harris in the White House, ensuring a Senate majority that will end the filibuster, and electing downballot Democrats and passing ballot initiatives to protect abortion rights and our democracy at the state level.
But we’re also keeping our eyes on the big picture: a democracy that reflects the will of the people. And we’ve got a roadmap.
This is worth fighting for — and I’m going to give this fight all that I’ve got. Thank you for being by my side.
[**We need to demonstrate that the American people are calling for these solutions. Please add your name if you agree with this plan to save our democracy.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-supcourt/?source=EMZ21E_JUD_E_20240627_V1S1&t=10&akid=2245%2E4032634%2EBrZMC7)
Thanks for being a part of this,
Elizabeth

Friend,

_**We live in an upside-down world. We're in a world where we blame victims and excuse criminals.**_

_**I served as King County Sheriff for eight years. I know how to hold criminals accountable.**_

Currently, in Washington, we have protestors blocking airports and freeways, along with daily car thefts and rising homelessness. Protestors have the right to express themselves, but _they DO NOT have the right to stomp on the rights of other people_.

The protestors blocked thousands of people who may have been headed to a medical appointment or a funeral.

_Washington has been struggling with rising crime and a shortage of police._ We need to create an environment where the criminal is held accountable, and police can make tough decisions and feel comfortable that the community has their back.

**As Sheriff, I served our community, and I recognize what we need now.** Members of our community are suffering. _They need our help._ I will do everything I can to ensure the homeless get off the street and receive the help they need.

I love America because my story is living proof that in the greatest country on Earth, anything is possible . body:
Rep. Susan Wild is the kind of fighter we need now more than ever.
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/9?t=1&akid=38943%2E3422442%2EG1Tiuz)
Derek—it’s Katie Porter.
During my three terms in Congress, I got to know _a lot_ of folks. Some of them are in Washington for the right reasons. Some...not so much. And some, like my friend Rep. Susan Wild, are the reason I can sleep soundly at night.
Susan is a champion for working people. She’s getting things done. She’s not afraid to stand up to special interests. **I’ll put it this way, Derek: She’s the kind of Congressperson that we need now more than ever.**
But Susan represents an *_extremely_ * competitive district, and we’re at real risk of losing her—especially if she doesn’t hit her fundraising goal before this week’s critical end-of-quarter deadline.
**[That’s why I’m asking you to split a donation between Susan’s campaign and my organization, Truth to Power, today.](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ttp-em-20240627-wild?refcode=em20240627-38943&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&refcode2=38943_3422442_G1Tiuz&akid=38943%2E3422442%2EG1Tiuz)**
[Donate ›››](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ttp-em-20240627-wild?refcode=em20240627-38943&refcode2=38943_3422442_G1Tiuz&akid=38943%2E3422442%2EG1Tiuz)
Susan’s district, the Pennsylvania 7th, is one of the most competitive in the country. In 2022, she won her race by just 2%. And this year, the NRCC is going to do everything it can to flip this seat from blue to red.
If they’re successful, we won’t just lose Susan’s critical voice. The reality is that without this seat, Democrats stand almost no chance at taking that Speaker’s gavel back from Mike Johnson. **But if Susan hits her end-of-quarter fundraising goal before this week’s deadline,_she’ll be in a better position to win in November._**

Friend --
Sometimes it shocks me that anyone donates to fundraising emails from political campaigns.
If you're anything like me, you open your email in the morning and it's overflowing with emails from every Senate campaign, House campaign, the presidential campaign, party committees, and organizations you know and likely many you've never heard of. Most of the time I haven’t signed up for these lists.
I get why these emails happen: they are an increasingly important part of how campaigns and organizations are funded. Especially on the Democratic side. Our small dollar, online, and texting programs are light-years more productive than the GOP, and often account for a third of our monthly fundraising.
So in a sea of Democratic emails and texts, I do my best to differentiate our content, and edit every single one, including this one. The fact that you opened this email instead of deleting it and made it this far gives me hope there's a chance.
There is no winning the Senate without this race in Michigan. There is no winning the White House either. At the same time, this is going to be one of the most competitive (and expensive) races in the country. Poll after poll shows it razor tight.
Republicans know that too, that is why they'll put ridiculous amounts of money in to beat us. And since I don’t accept corporate PAC money, I have to rely on the generosity of individuals like you who understand the stakes of this race.
Hopefully that's a compelling case. It’s my job to make it. Because there's no winning this race without a significant response to emails like this by people like you.

| Dear Kansan,

__Under President Trump, inflation never topped an annual rate of 2.4%. Two years into President Biden’s term in office, **inflation reached 9.1%** , a 40-year high__ _. _
__Under President Trump, the 30-year fixed mortgage rate was as low as 2.65%. Under President Biden, it has been as high as 8%. For the average Kansas homeowner, that’s a difference of **more than $300,000 in interest payments over 30 years**__ _._

__In the first two years of President Biden’s term in office, **gas prices doubled**__ _._
To make matters worse, we have the worst border crisis in American history, we’re $34 trillion in debt, and our Constitutional rights are being violated every day by big government overreach into our private lives.
**_This is madness, and it needs to stop_**. President Biden has proven that he cannot be trusted with America’s economy, national security, or Bill of Rights.
**_Now is the time to act – America’s future hangs in the balance_**.
I am asking you to join me in the fight to save our country by making a contribution before the end of the month. With your support, we can protect America’s future for our children and our grandchildren.

Yours in the fight,

Tracey Mann

clean_body: America was safer, stronger, and more prosperous before President Biden took office | | | | | | Dear Kansan, I don’t need to tell you that America was safer, stronger, and more prosperous before President Biden took office. The numbers speak for themselves. Under President Trump, inflation never topped an annual rate of 2.4%. Two years into President Biden’s term in office, inflation reached 9.1% , a 40-year high . Under President Trump, the 30-year fixed mortgage rate was as low as 2.65%. Under President Biden, it has been as high as 8%. For the average Kansas homeowner, that’s a difference of more than $300,000 in interest payments over 30 years . In the first two years of President Biden’s term in office, gas prices doubled . To make matters worse, we have the worst border crisis in American history, we’re $34 trillion in debt, and our Constitutional rights are being violated every day by big government overreach into our private lives. This is madness, and it needs to stop. President Biden has proven that he cannot be trusted with America’s economy, national security, or Bill of Rights. Now is the time to act – America’s future hangs in the balance. I am asking you to join me in the fight to save our country by making a contribution before the end of the month. With your support, we can protect America’s future for our children and our grandchildren. You can ( ) or visit my website at to learn more or contribute online. Let's fire Biden, restore the American dream, and bring real leadership back to our country. Yours in the fight, Tracey Mann P.S. We want to tell you a bit about Congressman Mark Green's story and why it is so crucial that we support him in his re-election campaign. **[Life of Service](https://click.historyoftheday.com/u/click?_t=930f96a60371422687dbefcfca24c32b&_m=753da732afa84b06ac45abc634401dae&_e=FiCwPh71ZoXcrD-o3tttc8OEVnbUKCgA0Ztx8KgNCGqd9yrqI-zsyuexGiqaEpk66KH2s82A7PrpfJHmSc2mzMSkmgh1qARHICCjjRtp3d32bbD2ifFDdixiYYd_V6aZGvVXBwXk8wReTCDz5bs1JluZXeyCWBE9T0idUDcXVxjFMb-jmx6n8ceZej6rUGPxvEnl62JJe-m49S_jUfBBL0aqcZjOCbfnIOlxDcmnXCWOCFHkszwyRT3AVyNDK_HUPxaUbJ6TYvN7IprYbFbQV9mwhKcBD1CBY0B1_aaAl2q1tOUsdvpVzZp0RTOVlNozYJn_e3V1eIRru3T_NWao2YpicNNzgjxUos8dM1dIcFWciddRdBzHCgiZ6lGpt21F)** [](https://click.historyoftheday.com/u/click?_t=930f96a60371422687dbefcfca24c32b&_m=753da732afa84b06ac45abc634401dae&_e=FiCwPh71ZoXcrD-o3tttc8OEVnbUKCgA0Ztx8KgNCGqd9yrqI-zsyuexGiqaEpk66KH2s82A7PrpfJHmSc2mzMSkmgh1qARHICCjjRtp3d32bbD2ifFDdixiYYd_V6aZGvVXBwXk8wReTCDz5bs1JluZXeyCWBE9T0idUDcXVxjFMb-jmx6n8ceZej6rUGPxvEnl62JJe-m49S_jUfBBL0aqcZjOCbfnIOlxDcmnXCVVZ27qFFXGGY63euxF3JRdJFSCsjBLzJlv5AE78PZ6pusiIjHoRPzuAR4QuPRQvDa6pBwN5gwO-afCsKx-jIIH5GuSCNn_sdvvE82zAcGs-GmqtCBrmhCdLPaq4VELIUXjMtDJRyesDSucaeEf04wx)
Dr. Mark Green was sworn in as Congressman from the 7th District of Tennessee on January 3rd, 2019. A physician, businessman, and combat veteran, Mark's life of service to the country began on the Plain at West Point at the age of 17. He decided to run for office during his 25th class reunion at the U.S. Military Academy at West Point. Seeing again the words on the statue of Gen. Douglas MacArthur, "Duty, honor, country," Mark realized that he had a duty to fulfill.

Between my and my wife’s service to our country, we’ve sacrificed years of our lives to make America a more safe and prosperous nation and to protect our God-given freedoms and liberties. We served so that our children and yours might grow up to realize their own American Dream. My name is Tim Sheehy, Republican candidate for U.S. Senate from Montana. I’m a former U.S. Navy SEAL and a 2008 Naval Academy graduate. Right now, I'm the only person standing in the way of Chuck Schumer and his Senate majority. With the most recently released poll indicating that Jon Tester and I are TIED at 46% each, your personal endorsement is more important now more than ever. In August 2021, I was putting out wildfires by day as part of the aerial firefighting company that I run; by night, my colleagues [many veterans like me] and I were working the phones trying to get our friends and allies out of Afghanistan before the takeover by the Taliban. I remember vividly trying to help an ally sneak through a tunnel to get him and his family to the airport so that they could be evacuated on a U.S. military aircraft. Let's recap, Peter...

* I’m the America First conservative and political outsider running to defeat 50-year career politician Shady Sherrod Brown in **Ohio’s toss-up U.S. Senate race.**

* **President Donald Trump won Ohio in 2016 and 2020** , making it one of our best chances to flip a seat red in 2024.

* Democrats have a 2-seat majority, which means **we MUST flip Ohio** in order to restore a Republican majority that can work with a Trump White House to get our country back on track.

* **President Trump has endorsed my campaign** , and it’s been my privilege to campaign alongside him.

* The latest polls show Brown with a **5% lead** , just outside the margin of error.

* Brown is also leading _**ALL U.S. SENATE CANDIDATES**_ in fundraising, making ours one of the biggest challenges to overcome.

I hope you understand _**we have no choice**_ but to win this seat in Ohio. _But I’m behind_ – both in polling and fundraising.

I can’t win in Ohio unless I receive the same support _(or more)_ from you and our conservative grassroots base that Sherrod Brown is from his leftist base.

Thankfully, we still have time to catch up. _But it’s going to take all of us pulling together!_

**Please show your commitment to delivering a Republican Senate majority for President Trump in 2024 by following his lead and sending support to our campaign.**

Bernie was born in Bogota, Colombia. At age five, his American Dream began when he moved to the United States with his family. Bernie became an American citizen at age 18.

Through his relentless work ethic and untamable entrepreneurial spirit, he turned the first car dealership that he purchased in 2005 into one of the largest dealership groups in America.

In 2016, Bernie recognized the value and transformational potential of blockchain technology, before it received mainstream attention, and moved much of his volunteer time and investment dollars into the space. In 2018 he co-founded ChampTitles, which grew to be quite successful as Bernie served as Chairman of the Board.

Since arriving in Congress, I was proud to cosponsor the _Respect for Marriage Act_ that was signed into law by President Biden. That legislation officially protects same-sex and interracial marriages nationwide.
**There is still so much work to do.** We still need to pass the _Equality Act_ to outlaw discrimination on the basis of gender or sexual orientation and protect access to housing, employment, credit, education, public spaces and services, and federal programs.
**It is hard to believe that such discrimination is still legal in the United States, but if we can protect my seat in CT-05 and flip the House majority, we _can_ pass the _Equality Act._**

name: Team Moore
subject: Obergefell v. Hodges
body:
Friend, as Pride month comes to a close, this moment calls for reflection on the history of what Pride means, how we can keep fighting for equality, and the importance of celebrating and acknowledging Pride all year long.

Just nine years ago, on June 26, 2015, the Supreme Court legalized same-sex marriage. After decades of activism, this was a hard-fought win for the LGBTQIA+ community.

While we should celebrate this major win, we also should not turn a blind eye to the constant attacks on the community that still occur to this day.

There is one thing we know: Maryland is a safe haven for the LGBTQIA+ community. Wes is determined to ensure Maryland remains the welcoming state it is and continue to remove the barriers that hold back our LGBTQIA+ neighbors from living their fullest lives.

Wes was the first governor in Maryland’s history to proclaim Transgender Day of Visibility in Maryland and signed the Trans Health Equity Act that delivers new funding for transitional housing for LGBTQ+ youth. He also signed an executive order that protects access to gender-affirming health care in Maryland, safeguarding the rights of individuals seeking, receiving, or providing gender-affirming care in Maryland from attempts at legal punishment by other states.

Wes also, for the first time since 2013, proclaimed June 2023 as LBGTQIA+ Pride Month in Maryland.

While June is dedicated to celebrating Pride, we know that this is more than just a month. Fighting for the LGBTQIA+ community happens all year long. Wes is dedicated to the mission of making Maryland the state where everyone can feel safe and free to be their most authentic selves.

[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP30/1/90457/images/IMG_0509.jpg]

Happy Pride, Maryland.

In solidarity,
Team Moore

name: Heidi Ganahl
subject: The Mountain Minute: 6/27/2024
body:
Your daily rundown of REAL news for REAL Coloradans.
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hi friends,
Our Editor and Publisher Brian Porter has been hard at work the last couple of days to make sure you are fully informed on the primary results, and equipped with crucial information as we head into the generals. Today's edition of the Mountain Minute features [ALL original content](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) from Brian, himself. We are so proud to have him on the RMV team!
We hope you enjoyed our live tweeting of the primary election results. We'll see you again LIVE tonight for the first presidential debate over on [X/Twitter](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)! Also, rather than our "Only on Rocky Mountain Voice" section of this newsletter, we've included articles relevant to tonight's debate (**scroll to the bottom**).
This is the Mountain Minute for Thursday, June 27, 2024.
- Heidi Ganahl
---
|
---
| | **TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
---
**[NRCC will invest $2.327 million in 8th District ad buy to support Evans](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
How much ad space will $2.327 million buy in the Denver market? If you reside in or near the 8th District, you are about to find out.
The National Republican Congressional Committee, fresh off Gabe Evans 55-point win in the primary election, announced Thursday the reinforcements are coming in an effort to prevent Democrat Yadira Caraveo's re-election.
The $2.327 million is third, falling behind NRCC investments of $2.5 million in Los Angeles, Calif., and $6/06 million in Portland, Ore.
"In 2023, the NRCC set a goal to expand the House Republican Majority by recruiting top tier candidates in Democrat-held seats, while at the same time shoring up our most vulnerable members," NRCC Independent Expenditure Director Tom Erickson wrote in a press statement.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**['The numbers don't lie', Boebert victory was a landslide in 4th District](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Lauren Boebert defeated all five Republican suitors in the 4th District's primary election for the U.S. House seat formerly held by ex-U.S. Rep. Ken Buck by 29.1% -- in a six-candidate race. For perspective, Boebert beat a field of five Republican opponents by a greater margin than Buck defeated one Democrat in his last general election.
* She ran as "100% conservative" and often noted proof such as an A-plus grade with the National Rifle Association and Gun Owners of America, and a 100% grade on the Liberty Scorecard. Half the field of candidates in the 4th District had failing Liberty grades.
* Other congressional races saw a similar trend: Jeff Hurd, an attorney and native of the 3rd District, collected 41.3% of all votes in another six-candidate field on Tuesday evening. Jeff Crank collected 65.2% of votes cast in the CD5 primary. And Gabe Evans defeated Janak Joshi by 55.1% to claim victory in the 8th District primary election.
* "The people have spoken," Boebert said. "They do not want a uniparty, but they do want a unified Republican Party."

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Could'Mighty 19′ grow and end Democrats' State House majority? Leadership hopes so.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Colorado House Republicans, known as the "Mighty 19," aim to increase their seats after strong showings in 10 contested primaries out of 65 seats.

* They need to gain at least three seats to break the Democrats' supermajority and 14 to regain control of the House.

* Several leadership changes are upcoming, with Minority Whip Richard Holtorf and former House Minority Leader Mike Lynch not returning, having sought other offices.

* Key primary wins by Republicans like Mary Bradfield and Kathy Reeves have bolstered confidence in challenging Democratic dominance.

* Republican leaders express optimism about introducing common-sense solutions and providing significant relief for Coloradans in the upcoming general elections.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Who voted in the primary? What a look inside the numbers tell us.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Younger voters largely abstained, with those aged 18 to 34 contributing only 7.0% of total ballots, as older generations, particularly ages 65-74, led in participation.
* Overall, 25.9% of Colorado's 3,872,503 registered voters participated in the primaries, with those aged 45 and older casting 79.1% of all ballots.
* Unaffiliated voters, the largest group, had a 19.2% turnout, evenly splitting their ballots between major parties.
* Republican turnout was estimated at 29.8%, slightly higher than the statewide average, with notable participation from older demographics.
* Female voters aged 65-74 were the most active demographic, and generally, more Democratic ballots were returned by females, while males returned more Republican ballots.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**['You can pick up the phone and fix it': Sonnenberg inspired to remain Eastern Plains commissioner](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Jerry Sonnenberg was the first and only opponent at the time to congratulate Lauren Boebert after she won the Republican primary for Colorado's 4th District, showcasing sportsmanship despite finishing second.
* Boebert won decisively with 43.4% of the vote, carrying 15 counties, while Sonnenberg secured 14.5% and won five counties.
* Sonnenberg expressed contentment with his role as county commissioner, highlighting his direct impact on community issues.
* Both Boebert and Sonnenberg hinted at a potential collaborative relationship moving forward, with Boebert appreciating Sonnenberg's gesture to retract a campaign tweet he found too harsh.
* Boebert called for unity within the Republican Party as they face the Democrats in the upcoming general election, while Sonnenberg showed openness to working together.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Looking ahead: The major-party general election matchups setup Tuesday night by primary voters](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
Voters in both the Democratic and Republican Party's primary elections weighed in and Tuesday night their general election nominees were selected.
There were two races at the top of the ballot with six candidates, while other top-line races were head-to-head and in some cases unopposed. The nominees now advance to the general election.
**[Click here](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** for a glance at how the major party's general election nominees will matchup in opposed races, assuming winners in preliminary returns stand.
|
---
**PRESIDENTIAL DEBATE COVERAGE ⤵️**
The first meeting on a debate stage of candidates for President in 2024 will be tonight. Donald Trump, President from 2017-20, and Joe Biden, President from 2020-present, will meet in advance of either party's national convention as the presumed nominees of their parties. **See below to links of interest in advance of the debate, and get your popcorn ready!** ****
**[The NY Post has created a drinking game (which we don't endorse) for the first Biden-Trump debate](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [NEW YORK POST](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) _The bar is officially open. President Biden and Donald Trump are squaring off in the first of two scheduled presidential debates Thursday, and The Post wants you to liven the night up with our official drinking game._
**[Not a toss-up: Polling guru Nate Silver gives Trump 66% chance of winning 2024 race](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [THE WASHINGTON TIMES](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) _Election prognosticator Nate Silver is no fan of Donald Trump, but he predicts that the former president will win the November election against President Biden, and what 's more, it won't be particularly close._
**[Kittle: Which Joe Biden will show up to debate Trump?](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [THE FEDERALIST](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) _It 's debate day. Insanely early (the contestants have yet to be nominated), but debate day nonetheless. It's Rocky versus Apollo. The rematch. Or more like Rocky versus Mickey -- if Rocky's elderly trainer had been reduced to a senile stooge in the throes of dementia, better suited for an assisted living facility than the boxing ring._ __

**Feel like you have a unique story or commentary to share?** We'd love to talk with you about becoming an RMV Contributor. Reply to this email (or reach out to [brian@rockymountainvoice.com](mailto:brian@rockymountainvoice.com?subject=Contributor%20Interest%20\(via%20Mountain%20Minute\)) or send us a message on social media to chat!
|
---
**🧐 DID YOU KNOW?** **In the early years of the United States, presidential candidates considered it unseemly to campaign, let alone debate their opponents.** Not until Democratic Senator John F. Kennedy and Republican Vice President Richard Nixon met in a Chicago television studio on September 26, 1960, did the major parties' nominees square off.

Despite the enormous audiences for the Kennedy-Nixon encounters, 16 years would go by before the next series of presidential debates. President Lyndon Johnson refused to debate in 1964, while Nixon did the same in 1968 and 1972.

Boebert won decisively with 43.4% of the vote, carrying 15 counties, while Sonnenberg secured 14.5% and won five counties. Sonnenberg expressed contentment with his role as county commissioner, highlighting his direct impact on community issues. Both Boebert and Sonnenberg hinted at a potential collaborative relationship moving forward, with Boebert appreciating Sonnenberg's gesture to retract a campaign tweet he found too harsh. Boebert called for unity within the Republican Party as they face the Democrats in the upcoming general election, while Sonnenberg showed openness to working together. | Voters in both the Democratic and Republican Party's primary elections weighed in and Tuesday night their general election nominees were selected. There were two races at the top of the ballot with six candidates, while other top-line races were head-to-head and in some cases unopposed. The nominees now advance to the general election. for a glance at how the major party's general election nominees will matchup in opposed races, assuming winners in preliminary returns stand. | PRESIDENTIAL DEBATE COVERAGE ⤵️ The first meeting on a debate stage of candidates for President in 2024 will be tonight. Donald Trump, President from 2017-20, and Joe Biden, President from 2020-present, will meet in advance of either party's national convention as the presumed nominees of their parties. See below to links of interest in advance of the debate, and get your popcorn ready! The bar is officially open. President Biden and Donald Trump are squaring off in the first of two scheduled presidential debates Thursday, and The Post wants you to liven the night up with our official drinking game. Election prognosticator Nate Silver is no fan of Donald Trump, but he predicts that the former president will win the November election against President Biden, and what 's more, it won't be particularly close. It 's debate day. Insanely early (the contestants have yet to be nominated), but debate day nonetheless. It's Rocky versus Apollo. The rematch. Or more like Rocky versus Mickey -- if Rocky's elderly trainer had been reduced to a senile stooge in the throes of dementia, better suited for an assisted living facility than the boxing ring. __ Feel like you have a unique story or commentary to share? We'd love to talk with you about becoming an RMV Contributor. Reply to this email (or reach out to mailto:brian@rockymountainvoice.com?subject=Contributor%20Interest%20\(via%20Mountain%20Minute\) or send us a message on social media to chat! | 🧐 DID YOU KNOW? In the early years of the United States, presidential candidates considered it unseemly to campaign, let alone debate their opponents. Not until Democratic Senator John F. Kennedy and Republican Vice President Richard Nixon met in a Chicago television studio on September 26, 1960, did the major parties' nominees square off. Despite the enormous audiences for the Kennedy-Nixon encounters, 16 years would go by before the next series of presidential debates. President Lyndon Johnson refused to debate in 1964, while Nixon did the same in 1968 and 1972. | CARTOON OF THE DAY | | QUOTE OF THE DAY** "To argue with a person who has renounced the use of reason is like administering medicine to the dead." -- Thomas Paine | Make sure to follow us on social media to stay in the loop on all things RMV 📲 | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|--- Did a friend forward you this email? | A product of Rocky Mountain Voice, Inc. 8200 S Quebec St, STE A3601 Centennial, CO 80112 This message was originally sent to: dpwillis67@gmail.com Be sure to put "RockyMountainVoice.com" on your safe-senders whitelist. June 27, 2024
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
CONTACT: Houston Keene
press@nancyforalaska.com

Nancy Dahlstrom Statement on First Presidential Debate

ANCHORAGE, AK - After tonight's disastrous debate performance by Joe
Biden, Mary Peltola and the Democrats are likely scrambling to pick up
the presidential pieces. Their worst nightmare just came true: Alaskans
and Americans couldn't be fooled any longer about their candidate.
President Donald J. Trump ran circles around Biden as the choice
between the prosperity of the previous administration and the failure
of the current could not be more clear.

In response to tonight's debate performance, Lt. Governor Nancy
Dahlstrom issued the following statement:

"Tonight's debate had one clear winner: President Donald J. Trump.
President Trump outperformed Joe Biden across every metric while the
Democrats' preferred candidate showcased the growing cracks in his
decades-old political facade," Lt. Governor Nancy Dahlstrom said in a
statement. "There's one question every American is asking following
this debate: can America afford another four years of Joe Biden
Commander-in-Chief? The answer is no, and we saw that on full display
tonight."

Ryan Mackenzie for U.S. Congress | | | | |
---
| Friends,
#TeamMackenzie is working harder than ever as we fight to offer real, honest representation to the people of the Lehigh Valley. To win, and deliver that change, we’re informing voters all across our community about Ryan’s proven record of results on real issues like protecting taxpayers and standing up to illegal immigration, and contrasting it with our opponent’s “say one thing at home, do something different in DC” record.
**Here are a couple of highlights from the campaign this week:**
* U.S. Chamber of Commerce endorsement
* NRCC Battle Station opening
* Schnecksville Fair

As always, if you need to get in contact with the campaign, please feel free to reach out to info@mackenzieforcongress.com
---
|
---
| **U.S. Chamber of Commerce Endorsement**
Job-creating businesses are the backbone of our economy and their success is the key to helping workers reach financial security for themselves and their families. As I have done as a state representative — and as too many in Washington have failed to do — I will support the commonsense policies that help these businesses thrive, grow our economy, and provide the good-paying jobs Americans need. I’m proud that the US Chamber has recognized my record and my commitment to a stronger future for American businesses.
---
|
---
| **NRCC Battle Station Now Open**
#TeamMackenzie is excited to announce the opening of the new National Republican Congressional Committee (NRCC) “Battle Station.” This office will be the headquarters for the Mackenzie campaign and shows just how focused the NRCC is on winning this race. We had an overflow crowd of supporters at the grand opening who came out to give their time and effort to bringing new leadership to the Lehigh Valley.
Volunteers continue to man the HQ and perform the grassroots activities that will help us win! Join them today: [https://www.mackenzieforcongress.com/#Volunteer](https://mackenzieforcongress.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=62252a4538e3fe848298033c5&id=6d159ed262&e=5ccada9200)
---
|
---
| **Schnecksville Fair**
This week I joined volunteers at the Schnecksville Fair. As we visit events throughout the district, we run into more and more voters who are tired of the failed leadership that’s coming from our out-of-touch congresswoman. Voters are ready for a change, and we’re excited to offer it.
---
|
---

As the Biden-Wild record continues to fall apart and our polling surges, we have our best chance ever. Hi friends.
OK – let’s talk about why your inbox is filled with political fundraising emails right now, because there is a real reason (and it’s actually very important).
June 30th marks the end of the second quarter of the year, and is also the date of a major Federal Election Commission deadline for candidates across the country. Basically, any money that candidates raise across the entirety of Q2 – from 12:01 AM on April 1st through 11:59 PM on June 30th – has to be filed with the FEC, and then those reports are made public for anyone to see.
This matters for so many reasons , but one of the most important factors is that these public FEC reports demonstrate the state of the race to anyone who cares to look – reporters, campaign teams, activists, candidates themselves.
When our report comes out, you better believe my opponent and his team will be scrutinizing it and making their own strategic decisions based on what they see there.
And it’s pretty straightforward: A weak report signifies that the campaign may be weak as well, and can lead to major attacks from the other side once they smell blood in the water.
We already know that my opponent can raise serious money around his MAGA politics and anti-abortion mission. In one recent filing, he reported more than half a million dollars raised – so we can’t afford to get complacent here.
That’s why I’m coming to you today. I work hard to raise funds for my campaign across a wide variety of sources, from events to phone calls to pitching in my own personal resources – but nothing can replace having grassroots support .
Showing that there’s enthusiasm on the ground for my re-election campaign is really important to securing a strong Democratic victory in November. Will you help out by pitching in $10, $20, or whatever amount is meaningful to you before our June 30th FEC deadline? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em]
If you’ve saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:

OTHER [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em]
Thank you so much for reading and for your support. I appreciate you!
-Sara

With the most recently released poll indicating that Jon Tester and I are TIED at 46% each, your personal endorsement is more important now more than ever. In August 2021, I was putting out wildfires by day as part of the aerial firefighting company that I run; by night, my colleagues [many veterans like me] and I were working the phones trying to get our friends and allies out of Afghanistan before the takeover by the Taliban. I remember vividly trying to help an ally sneak through a tunnel to get him and his family to the airport so that they could be evacuated on a U.S. military aircraft. The Taliban wanted these high-value targets dead; they wanted their families dead. Unlike Joe Biden, I understand what it is to serve our country. Not service in politics, but on the battlefield. I’ve been wounded in service of our nation; I’ve lost mentors and friends who were willing to make the ultimate sacrifice so that future generations will be free. Chuck Schumer and Washington Democrats know that I pose a direct threat to their chances of holding on to power, and they'll do anything to stop me from winning this race - and spend $100M plus in the process. Peter, I am under no illusions that you will support my campaign each time you hear from me. But my life experiences have taught me that anything worth having requires working tirelessly, breaking down walls, and moving mountains to get it. I hope you will allow me to earn your support today by reading my entire message - I promise, it’s worth the read. On the battlefield, finding yourself between a rock and a hard place is easy. This rings especially true for the highly trained combat warriors I served alongside as a Navy SEAL. Being a SEAL isn’t a one-man job; it takes teamwork, problem-solving, and coming to a consensus. When you’re on missions in the harshest environments known to man, you must act as a unit and recognize you’re only as strong as the weakest among you. I’ve deployed to Iraq, Afghanistan, South America, and the Pacific during my time as a SEAL, and I have been involved in dozens of engagements with enemy forces and survived to tell the tales. And believe me, there are some tales. I’ve seen the world’s dangers and stood up for freedom in the face of terrorism. I know the strength it takes to stand up and fight for what is right – which is why Our homeland is in danger. Radical Democrats in Washington want to fundamentally alter the fabric of this GREAT nation. This FAR-LEFT liberal agenda is assaulting our society, communities, and the American Dream. The Democrats’ grip on power is seriously undermining our freedom, prosperity, and security. The only way to flip the Senate this year is to nominate a strong conservative candidate who can defeat my liberal Democrat opponent in less than five months. Over the weeks ahead leading up to the election, you’ll receive emails from me and my team as we work to defeat entrenched liberal Senator Jon Tester. While I don’t want you to feel obligated to interact with each piece of content you receive in your inbox, I kindly ask you to refrain from unsubscribing from our contact list. The only way to flip the Senate this year is if we are all working toward the same mission. *If we fail to flip this Montana seat RED this November, we lose our best chance at a Senate Majority for the next DECADE due to the election map at play. This is my most critical mission to date, and Thank you, Tim Sheehy Former Navy SEAL Republican Candidate for U.S. Senate For America's Future, Tim Sheehy Republican for U.S. Senate, Montana | " "I SERVED AS A NAVY SEAL, BUILT ONE OF THE LARGEST AERIAL FIREFIGHTING COMPANIES IN AMERICA CREATING OVER 200 MONTANA JOBS, AND STARTED A VETERAN-LED CATTLE RANCHING AND FEEDING OPERATION. WHETHER IT WAS IN WAR OR BUSINESS, I SEE PROBLEMS AND SOLVE THEM. AMERICA NEEDS CONSERVATIVE LEADERS WHO LOVE OUR COUNTRY. I'M RUNNING FOR THE U.S. SENATE BECAUSE OUR CAMPAIGN IS ABOUT SERVICE, DUTY, AND COUNTRY -- NOT POLITICS AS USUAL." * | PAID FOR BY TIM SHEEHY FOR MONTANA Tim Sheehy is a former Navy SEAL. | | 2\. 14 Things You Can Do Right Now
---
| | Here is a list of ways you can communicate to your TV stations, radio stations, and newspapers that you want to see more pro-Biden content: 1\. Write Letters to the Editor: Most newspapers have a section for letters to the editor. Write a letter expressing your desire for more pro-Biden content and the reasons why you believe it is important.2\. Email News Outlets: Send emails to the news directors or editors of your local TV stations, radio stations, and newspapers. Clearly state your request for more pro-Biden coverage and provide examples of the types of stories you'd like to see.3\. Call Newsrooms: Call the newsrooms of your local media outlets and ask to speak with someone in charge of content or editorial decisions. Express your views and make a case for why more pro-Biden content is needed.4\. Use Social Media: Tag TV stations, radio stations, and newspapers on social media platforms like Twitter, Facebook, and Instagram. Publicly request more pro-Biden content and encourage others to do the same. Use relevant hashtags to increase visibility.5\. Submit Feedback Through Websites: Many media outlets have feedback forms on their websites. Use these forms to request more pro-Biden content and explain why it matters to you.6\. Participate in Audience Surveys: When TV and radio stations or newspapers conduct audience surveys, make sure to participate and clearly state your preference for more pro-Biden content.7\. Organize a Petition: Start an online petition calling for more pro-Biden coverage and share it with your network. Once you have gathered enough signatures, present it to the media outlets.8\. Join or Form Advocacy Groups: Join local advocacy groups or form one with like-minded individuals to collectively request more pro-Biden content. A group effort can often have more impact than individual requests.9\. Attend Public Meetings: If your local media outlets hold public meetings or forums, attend and voice your opinion on the need for more pro-Biden content.10\. Advertise Your Support: If possible, buy ad space in newspapers or airtime on radio stations to publicly express your support for Biden and advocate for more positive coverage.11\. Write Opinion Pieces: Submit opinion pieces or guest columns to local newspapers outlining the positive aspects of Biden’s policies and leadership, and the need for more balanced reporting.12\. Support Pro-Biden Media: Subscribe to and financially support media outlets that already provide pro-Biden content. Encourage your network to do the same and let the outlets know why you’re supporting them.13\. Engage with Advertisers: Contact advertisers that support the media outlets and let them know you appreciate their support but would like to see more pro-Biden content. Advertisers have significant influence over media content.14\. Provide Pro-Biden Content: Offer to provide content or contribute to local media outlets with pro-Biden articles, interviews, or commentary pieces. By using these methods, you can effectively communicate your desire for more pro-Biden content to your local media outlets.

| | 5\. Duane Pitts: I Remember Korea
---
| | Originally published on June 25, 2024, by private email, reprinted with permission from the author, Duane Pitts. On this date 74 years ago, the United States entered the Korean War on the side of what would become South Korea. Our parents lived in Fukuoka, Japan at the time. Dad was a Sgt in the Combat Engineers (CE) Division of the US Army stationed in Japan. His job switched from training in pontoon building to building roads and bridges, pontoon or otherwise, to aid US and South Korean troops in their movements to stop the communists from running over southern Korea. His unit was one of the many who helped build the roads and bridges to the trapped US Marines at Choisin Reservoir. Once the troops got out of the trap the Chinese and north Koreans had set, Dad's unit had to destroy the bridges before the Chinese took them. He said they had only 2 rifles in his unit and each man had a side pistol. That was it for defense against the Chinese and north Koreans shooting at them! Dad told us many funny stories about the war, but only once did he talk with tears in his eyes. He lost his best buddy in the war. When they bivouacked once for the night, the unit split 50-50 on either side of a dry creek bed. A night guard was stationed as a precaution, as they were close to the fighting lines. That night, the guard and sleeping men in the other half of the unit on the opposite side of the creek had their throats slit. Morning revealed the massacre to the survivors. Quietly, Dad said he cried and cried as he held his best friend. That was all he would ever say about that terrible loss. Mom had trained for secretarial work, so during WW2 she worked in the secretarial pool for the British Consulate in Portland, Oregon. Long story short, they married in Elmhurst, a suburb near Chicago, in 1945. When Mom joined Dad in Japan in 1948, I was not yet one. When they lived in Fukuoka, Mom stayed home with me and my sister, who was born in 1949 in a US military hospital. They had seven Japanese maids and one Japanese gardener. Two US military guards were posted at the house, one during the day and the other at night, after the Korean War started in June of 1950. 9 days later I would turn 3. After the Korean War started, Mom applied for and got the job of main secretary to the Provost Marshall in Fukuoka. In this job, she was privy to US troop movements in Korea, all of Korea, so she was able to learn each day where Dad's CE unit was and if he were still alive. She saw the daily report of wounded and dead. Given the nature of her job, Mom could speak to no one about what she saw, read, heard in the Provost Marshall's office. She couldn't even tell other women who had a military spouse anything about their spouse or his whereabouts. Nothing. She said that was the most difficult part of the job. She cried many times, but only in the office. Me? What do I remember from the Korean War? One thing only about the war itself, which Mom explained to me. I heard thunder coming across the sky and water, loud thunder but no clouds. Mom told me that was the sound of war from Korea coming over the sea. I can still recall the sounds of that thunder rolling over Fukuoka. Other memories were of Dad's and Mom's stories told to me and my sister about our time in Japan during the Korean War. However, those are for another time and less important occasion. I remember Korea.

Duane Pitts: I Remember Korea | | Originally published on June 25, 2024, by private email, reprinted with permission from the author, Duane Pitts. On this date 74 years ago, the United States entered the Korean War on the side of what would become South Korea. Our parents lived in Fukuoka, Japan at the time. Dad was a Sgt in the Combat Engineers (CE) Division of the US Army stationed in Japan. His job switched from training in pontoon building to building roads and bridges, pontoon or otherwise, to aid US and South Korean troops in their movements to stop the communists from running over southern Korea. His unit was one of the many who helped build the roads and bridges to the trapped US Marines at Choisin Reservoir. Once the troops got out of the trap the Chinese and north Koreans had set, Dad's unit had to destroy the bridges before the Chinese took them. He said they had only 2 rifles in his unit and each man had a side pistol. That was it for defense against the Chinese and north Koreans shooting at them! Dad told us many funny stories about the war, but only once did he talk with tears in his eyes. He lost his best buddy in the war. When they bivouacked once for the night, the unit split 50-50 on either side of a dry creek bed. A night guard was stationed as a precaution, as they were close to the fighting lines. That night, the guard and sleeping men in the other half of the unit on the opposite side of the creek had their throats slit. Morning revealed the massacre to the survivors. Quietly, Dad said he cried and cried as he held his best friend. That was all he would ever say about that terrible loss. Mom had trained for secretarial work, so during WW2 she worked in the secretarial pool for the British Consulate in Portland, Oregon. Long story short, they married in Elmhurst, a suburb near Chicago, in 1945. When Mom joined Dad in Japan in 1948, I was not yet one. When they lived in Fukuoka, Mom stayed home with me and my sister, who was born in 1949 in a US military hospital. They had seven Japanese maids and one Japanese gardener. Two US military guards were posted at the house, one during the day and the other at night, after the Korean War started in June of 1950. 9 days later I would turn 3. After the Korean War started, Mom applied for and got the job of main secretary to the Provost Marshall in Fukuoka. In this job, she was privy to US troop movements in Korea, all of Korea, so she was able to learn each day where Dad's CE unit was and if he were still alive. She saw the daily report of wounded and dead. Given the nature of her job, Mom could speak to no one about what she saw, read, heard in the Provost Marshall's office. She couldn't even tell other women who had a military spouse anything about their spouse or his whereabouts. Nothing. She said that was the most difficult part of the job. She cried many times, but only in the office. Me? What do I remember from the Korean War? One thing only about the war itself, which Mom explained to me. I heard thunder coming across the sky and water, loud thunder but no clouds. Mom told me that was the sound of war from Korea coming over the sea. I can still recall the sounds of that thunder rolling over Fukuoka. Other memories were of Dad's and Mom's stories told to me and my sister about our time in Japan during the Korean War. However, those are for another time and less important occasion. I remember Korea. | | | | | Your generous support is the backbone of our efforts. Found it on Common Sense Weekly \(Subscribe here: \.) ---|--- | []() | ---|--- Kennedy's campaign gains ground in Pennsylvania, submitting double the required signatures for ballot access. This key swing state victory adds to the campaign's growing momentum across the nation.With ballot access secured or within reach in 23 states, totaling 323 electoral votes, RFK Jr. is proving to be a formidable independent candidate. Recent polls show RFK Jr. outperforming both Biden and Trump in head-to-head matchups, signaling a potential shake-up in the 2024 presidential race. | | | ---|--- | []() | ---|--- RFK Jr. showcases his progressive vision and environmental commitment at the premiere of Recovering America in New Mexico. The documentary highlights his efforts to address addiction and uplift marginalized communities. His focus on environmental protection aligns with NM's values, positioning him as a potential advocate for the state's natural treasures.RFK Jr.'s choice of New Mexico for the premiere demonstrates his engagement with diverse communities and local issues. As an independent candidate, his progressive platform and environmental stance offer voters an alternative to traditional party politics. | | | ---|--- | []() | ---|--- | Shape Tomorrow with RFK Jr: Your Voice, Your Vote Contribute to a brighter future through action:🗳️ Secure ballot access for RFK Jr across the nation.💡 Volunteer for a campaign that represents your values.🌍 Build a more inclusive, united future together.🤝 Join forces with fellow advocates in your community.🎉 Be part of a movement that fights for all Americans. | | | RFK Jr. talks about the troubling issue of corporate capture within legal systems, focusing on the case of Steve Donziger, an environmental lawyer facing legal backlash after winning a $10 billion lawsuit against Chevron for pollution in Ecuador. He exposes how big oil companies use legal systems to silence critics and avoid accountability. He calls for a presidential pardon for Donziger and urges support for a petition seeking his release.Why It Matters: This case exemplifies the broader issue of corporate influence on legal processes and the challenges environmental defenders face. | | | ---|--- | []() | ---|--- Are you ready to make a real difference and help drive positive change? They discuss environmental issues, such as water contamination from cobalt mining in Idaho, foreign ownership of farmland, and the lack of representation for family farms in Washington. Their conversation calls for agricultural policy reform, increased support for small farmers, and greater transparency in land ownership.Key Points: Shifting of agricultural subsidies toward large corporations contributes to the decline of family farms Increasing foreign ownership of U.S. farmland can impact national food and water security Having a national voice for small agricultural producers in Washington D.C. can resolve these issues | | | ---|--- | []() | ---|--- RFK Jr. presents his views on vaccines, particularly the COVID-19 vaccine, on the Young Turks show. He expresses skepticism about the pharmaceutical industry's influence on vaccine safety and questions the medical community's unanimous endorsement of vaccines.RFK Jr. challenges claims about the COVID-19 vaccine's transmission prevention abilities, citing scientific studies and global data. He calls for greater transparency, accountability, and legal recourse in vaccine safety, emphasizing individual choice and the need for rigorous scientific scrutiny. | | | ---|--- | []() | ---|--- Are you ready to make a real difference and help drive positive change? He criticizes overregulation that has pushed these industries overseas and calls for a president who understands and plans for their future.While acknowledging concerns about AI's impact on jobs, he sees its potential for prosperity and improved quality of life. His vision aims to position America at the forefront of these technologies while making sure they benefit the public and keep the government accountable. | | | ---|--- | []() | ---|--- Our weekly Thursday night calls start at 6:30pm EST with a 30 minute review that will catch up any newcomers to the call. clean_body: With Cori Bush's primary in Missouri just over 2 months away, we need to act fast to combat the waves upon waves of right-wing money headed her way. | | | Peter, We know who’s next in AIPAC’s sights:Rep. Cori Bush, whose opponent is among the top 4 recipients of AIPAC’s Republican megadonor cash this cycle. With Cori’s primary in Missouri just over 2 months away, we need to act fast to combat the waves upon waves of right-wing money headed her way. Which is why we’re asking one more time: This race is close, and every dollar we raise to support Cori’s campaign could make the difference. In solidarity, Team WFP \---------- Forwarded message --------- From: WFP Election Alert Date: June 26, 2024 Subject: Not the email we wanted to send Peter, Last night, Republican megadonors ousted a progressive champion. AIPAC and the Trump and GOP donors fueling their efforts spent more than $17 million to defeat Jamaal Bowman in a Democratic primary — making his race the most expensive House primary in history. Despite a powerful, multi-racial coalition coming together in defense of Rep. Bowman, that kind of onslaught of spending was simply too much to overcome last night. But it doesn’t have to be a sign of things to come. AIPAC’s next target is Rep. Cori Bush, who is already facing millions in attack ads from some of the same dark-money Super PACs. Cori is one of the few working-class members of Congress, a tireless champion for abortion rights, and was one of the first members to courageously call for a ceasefire in Gaza. All of that has painted a target on her back for the same Republican megadonors. Our opponents aren’t about to let up — and we can’t afford to either. Cori Bush’s primary in Missouri is just six weeks away, and if she wins, it would send a powerful message to the entire country. That’s why it’s so important for us to have her back right now in whatever way we can:** Just a few months ago, AIPAC promised to spend up to $100 million in 2024 to unseat the Squad from Congress.1 Since then, they have become the largest source of Republican donations in Democratic primaries.2 Their strategy was to try and divide us during this primary season and weaken our movement going into the fall, all so that they could achieve their ultimate goal come November: returning full control of Congress and the White House to Trump and MAGA Republicans. We can’t let them succeed. With the primary just six weeks away, and the attack ads already starting, Cori Bush has a plan to reach the voters she needs to reach in order to win — but that plan depends on all of us.
